A user torn on LLM code review saw Cursor Bugbot (and Claude) flag a bug and suggest a reasonable fix, then argue against that fix and ask for it to be reverted. After reverting, they got the exact same original recommendation again.

Workaround: worried the flip-flopping would become a circus for less experienced devs, a user turned off automatic Bugbot/LLM code reviews. They now trigger them on request via a GitHub Action to keep PR comment history from filling with verbose agent comments.

"Its live in our org and is actually pretty good, almost none of its comments are frivolous or wrong, and it finds genuine bugs most reviewers miss. This is unlike Graphite and Copilot... Bugbot is now a valuable part of our SD process."

Asked whether they had used Bugbot, a user said they assumed it was the code review comments Cursor spontaneously shows in the IDE "as part of some upsell," and that those comments "were all subtly wrong."
"I've found Bugbot to be shockingly effective at finding bugs in my PRs. Even when it's wrong, it's usually worth adding a comment, since it's the kind of mistake a human reviewer would make."
